 AST SpaceMobile shares jump ahead of Q3 results as dealmaking gathers pace 
 Published: 13:19 09 Nov 2026 EST
 AST SpaceMobile Inc (NASDAQ:ASTS) shares jumped 14% on Monday as investors weighed a series of strategic developments ahead of the satellite communications company's third-quarter earnings report due after the market close. 
 The rally follows the announcement of a joint venture with Japan's Rakuten to bring satellite-to-mobile connectivity to Japan, supported by up to US$1 billion in potential Japanese government funding. 
 AST has also struck a US$1.3 billion agreement with Firefly Aerospace to secure rocket engines and technology for its planned reusable Blacklift launch vehicle, marking a significant expansion of its ambitions to control more of its satellite deployment infrastructure. 
 Under the three-year agreement, Firefly will supply 27 Miranda and nine Vira engines for the first three rockets, provide engineering support and license the underlying technology. AST plans to manufacture the engines at a new US facility, with Blacklift targeting its first flight in late 2028. 
 UBS described the strategy as a potential hedge against long-term launch availability and a step towards greater vertical integration, but warned that it introduces significant execution risks. 
 The analysts noted that developing a reusable 20-tonne launch vehicle represents a substantial undertaking beyond AST's core satellite business. Additional spending on manufacturing facilities, launch infrastructure and staffing could also push costs beyond the announced US$1.3 billion commitment, with implications for capital expenditure and margins. 
 For now, AST will continue relying on external launch providers, having signed agreements covering the deployment of more than 100 satellites through 2028. 
 Execution remains an important consideration. UBS noted that AST had not launched a satellite in September or October, despite an earlier expectation of roughly one launch per month. The company is targeting 45 satellites in orbit by early 2027, compared with 12 currently. 
 Investors will also be looking for progress on commercial operations and revenue growth when AST reports its third-quarter results. 
 Consensus estimates point to revenue of approximately US$46 million, up from US$31.52 million in the second quarter, reflecting commercial gateway deliveries and milestone achievements. 
 The company has also reported successful network handoff tests with AT&T, demonstrating the ability to transition between conventional mobile networks and satellite connectivity without requiring specialized equipment.
